## Problem

A Kailash system (or any Linux box carrying its tooling) is in place.
The goal is one loop that proves the whole stack works. The loop:
serve a real model on a controlled port. Prove the endpoint is alive.
Point the flagship LLM scanner at it. Read an actual report — all in
one sitting, cheap enough to repeat after every change. This loop is
the operator version of the OS spec's own CI assertion. The CI side is
the O-4 tiny-local-model + A-2 garak integration, `nightly`.

## Solution

Both ends are manifest rows. Ollama (OPS, o-04, native, safety
`safe`) serves the target. Garak (ATTACK, a-02, bespoke, safety
`requires-target`) does the firing. Work the loop top to bottom:

```bash
# 1. Confirm both rows from the manifest view (also your first
#    `kailash info` run — see the CLI inventory recipe)
kailash info ollama   # -> OPS / o-04 / native / safety safe
kailash info garak    # -> ATTACK / a-02 / bespoke / requires-target

# 2. Pull the tiny test model (a sub-1B quant keeps every scan loop
#    short; the pull is roughly 0.7 GB of layers)
ollama pull smollm2:360m

# 3. Serve it bound to loopback ONLY — the blast-radius boundary
OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434 ollama serve

# 4. In a second terminal: prove health BEFORE the scanner touches it
curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/
curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate \
     -d '{"model":"smollm2:360m","prompt":"Reply with OK only.","stream":false}'

# 5. THE scan: OWASP-LLM01 scoped, 5 generations per probe, seeded for
#    reproducibility
garak --target_type ollama --target_name smollm2:360m \
      --spec tag:owasp:llm01 -g 5 -s 42

# 6. Read the run as a report (the JSONL file from step 5's banner)
garak --report garak_<timestamp>.jsonl
```

What success looks like:

- `ollama pull` ends with a `"success"` line for the tag
- `ollama list` shows `smollm2:360m` with a non-zero SIZE column
- the root endpoint answers `Ollama is running`
- the generate call returns one JSON object with a `response` field
  (streaming off)
- the scan prints its banner and `📜 reporting to garak_<ts>.jsonl`,
  then one progress line + per-detector scores per probe
- the seeded run (`-s 42`) reproduces the same probe/target
  interaction set. Re-run after any config change and diff the reports

Expected output shape (abridged — the scan leg, shapes not
transcripts):

```
garak LLM safety & security scanning tool v<version> ( https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak ) at <ISO timestamp>
📜 reporting to garak_<timestamp>.jsonl
...
🔍 probing <probe> (<n> generation(s))
   <detector>  passed  <n>/<m>
```

## Discussion

- **Why this loop is the baseline:** it is the smallest chain that
  exercises every layer contract at once. The chain spans a native
  OPS serving row (safety `safe`). It spans a bespoke ATTACK firing
  row (`requires-target`). The OWASP mapping (`LLM01` in both
  manifest epochs) does the scoping. After a rebuild, re-run steps
  4–6 as the smoke check.
- **Why loopback binding is mandatory:** a scan target is a deliberate
  attack surface. Garak drives the model with adversarial prompts by
  design. A `0.0.0.0` bind puts that surface on the network. Bind
  `127.0.0.1` and keep the target on the lab box.
- **Why the endpoint and generator agree by default:** garak's Ollama
  generator defaults its host to `127.0.0.1:11434`. That is the same
  loopback bind step 3 uses, so no extra wiring is needed. Move the
  port? Move both sides in the same change and re-verify health
  first.
- **Why `-g 5` and `-s 42`, and no more:** five generations per probe
  keep a scoped run quick, and the detectors still get samples. The
  seed makes the scan a regression test: change a system prompt or a
  guardrail, re-scan same-seed, diff. A first run answers one
  question — injection resistance (`tag:owasp:llm01`) — not the full
  catalogue. Scale up when a real engagement needs it.
- **The CI-side twin:** the spec's test chapter names
  `integration-garak-local` as the standing assertion of this
  pairing. The integration row: O-4 tiny local model + A-2 garak, one
  probe class, `nightly` flag. An operator who runs this recipe by
  hand can diff the results against the nightly record.
- **Alternate tiny model:** the o-04 module's notes name
  `qwen2.5:0.5b` (~0.4 GB, the module's primary operator example).
  `smollm2:360m` is the smaller-tag alternative. Any sub-1B quant
  works. Pick one and keep it pinned for the loop's baseline.

verified 2026-10-14 at main. The garak CLI surface
(`--target_type/--target_name/--spec/-g/-s`, `--report`) is verified
against upstream `garak/cli.py` at source HEAD and the packaged pin
**0.17.1.pre1-unstable-2026-10-09** (pin source: `pkgs/garak/default.nix`
+ `nvfetcher/_sources/generated.nix`); the Ollama generator's default
host `127.0.0.1:11434` is its `generators/ollama.py` contract. The
Ollama surfaces (`pull`, `OLLAMA_HOST`, `/`, `/api/generate`

registry-manifest sums (layer bytes at publish time; they move when
